incidents.vector: AI-assisted discovery and weaponization of a zero-day 2FA-bypass logic flaw in a Python administration script; exploit code carried tell-tale LLM artifacts including a hallucinated CVSS score.
incidents.impact: Google Threat Intelligence Group identified the bug and worked with the vendor on a patch before the planned mass exploitation campaign launched; assessed as the first publicly confirmed AI-developed zero-day weaponized by a cybercrime crew.

incidents.vector: Phishing email attachment in September 2020 gave the attacker a foothold; they used a domain administrator account and an unpatched ZeroLogon flaw to move laterally and lurked undetected until May 2022.
incidents.impact: UK ICO fined the utility £963,900 ($1.3M) after 4.1 TB of data on 633,887 customers and staff (names, addresses, bank account numbers, National Insurance numbers, disability indicators) was published. Operational/water-treatment systems were not affected. Regulator cited failures in least-privilege, vulnerability scanning, and SOC monitoring of only 5% of the estate.

incidents.vector: Two newly disclosed Linux kernel logic flaws — Copy Fail (CVE-2026-31431) in the AF_ALG crypto subsystem and Dirty Frag (CVE-2026-43284 / CVE-2026-43500) in kernel networking — allow unprivileged local users to overwrite the in-memory page cache of setuid binaries and escalate to root, enabling container escape.
incidents.impact: Affects nearly all Linux distributions since 2017; CISA added Copy Fail to the KEV catalog. Microsoft Defender is observing PoC testing activity; an unrelated party broke the Dirty Frag embargo on May 7, forcing public exploit release. Red Hat, AlmaLinux, Ubuntu and SUSE are racing out patches.

incidents.victim: Aerospace and drone operators (Russian government and enterprises)
incidents.vector: Phishing and malvertising delivering trojanized aviation software installers, JavaScript RAT, PowerShell scripts and LNK files abusing the ZDI-CAN-25373 Windows shortcut flaw; also planted a fake SourceForge project.
incidents.impact: Kaspersky-tracked group (HeartlessSoul / Versatile Werewolf, also tracked by Positive Technologies and BI.ZONE) has been exfiltrating GIS shapefiles, terrain models and GPS data from Russian government and industrial targets since September 2025, providing adversaries operational ground-truth on Russian infrastructure and logistics.

incidents.vector: Re-exploitation of an issue in Canvas Free-for-Teacher accounts (the same flaw used in the May 1 incident that Instructure had declared 'contained'); attackers defaced the Canvas login page with a ransom demand.
incidents.impact: Disrupted classes and exams at thousands of schools and universities during finals week; ShinyHunters claims data on 275M students and faculty across ~9,000 institutions including names, email addresses, student IDs and messages. Instructure pulled Canvas offline; sources tell Krebs multiple universities are negotiating ransoms independently.

incidents.vector: Rust-compiled fake ScreenConnect update drops a .NET loader that deploys 'CloudZ' RAT plus a new 'Pheno' plugin; plugin hijacks Microsoft Phone Link's PC-to-phone bridge to read the local SQLite database of synced SMS messages.
incidents.impact: Cisco Talos discovered active intrusions dating to at least January 2026 in which attackers harvest browser credentials and silently siphon SMS-delivered one-time passwords and authenticator notifications without touching the victim's phone — enabling MFA bypass against banking and corporate accounts.

incidents.victim: Government entities in South America and southeastern Europe
incidents.vector: Initial access (likely via zero-day or n-day exploits), followed by deployment of the .NET 'NetDraft' backdoor (a C# variant of the FinalDraft/SquidDoor family), CloudSorcerer v3, SNAPPYBEE/DeedRAT, ZingDoor, and SNOWLIGHT/VSHELL plus a new Rust stager 'SNOWRUST'.
incidents.impact: Cisco Talos disclosed long-running intrusions targeting government ministries in South America since late 2024 and southeastern Europe in 2025, aimed at long-term access, credential extraction and Active Directory enumeration. Tooling overlaps tie UAT-8302 to multiple China-nexus clusters.

incidents.victim: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS firewall operators
incidents.vector: Unauthenticated buffer-overflow zero-day (CVE-2026-0300) in PAN-OS User-ID Authentication (Captive) Portal; shellcode injected into nginx worker, followed by EarthWorm and ReverseSocks5 tunneling, SAML flood to fail-over to a second device, AD enumeration with the firewall service account, and systematic log destruction.
incidents.impact: Confirmed exploitation against an unnamed organization between April 9 and April 29, 2026. Palo Alto Networks issued an emergency advisory on May 6; Unit 42 assesses the operator demonstrated nation-state-grade tradecraft (open-source tooling, intermittent sessions, identity-trust abuse) consistent with edge-device prepositioning.

incidents.vector: Social-engineered DigiCert tech-support staff into running an SCR (Windows screensaver) file; one workstation had a CrowdStrike EDR agent misconfigured and disconnected from the management server, letting the attacker dwell almost two weeks and harvest EV-certificate 'initialization codes' from in-progress customer orders.
incidents.impact: Attackers obtained 27 EV code-signing certificates which were used to sign Zhong Stealer cryptocurrency-theft malware. DigiCert revoked all 60 EV certificates approved during the dwell window. Stolen certs were tied to GoldenEyeDog (APT-Q-27), although it is unclear if that group ran the DigiCert intrusion itself.

incidents.victim: cPanel / WHM shared hosting customers (including the Guam government and ~44,000 systems)
incidents.vector: Active in-the-wild exploitation of CVE-2026-41940, a critical authentication-bypass-to-RCE flaw in cPanel/WHM (affecting all versions after 11.40, released in 2013).
incidents.impact: ASD's ACSC issued a critical Australian alert May 1 confirming active exploitation. Per Censys/Shadowserver, more than 44,000 cPanel systems were compromised; attackers ran a 'Fakestortion' wave wiping public websites and posting bogus $8,000 BTC ransom demands, plus dropping cryptominers and DDoS payloads. Guam government sites were taken offline.

incidents.victim: Republican Party of Alberta voter rolls
incidents.vector: Personal data of 2.9 million Albertan voters was placed online in a public, searchable database maintained by the separatist Republican Party of Alberta — an exposure rather than an external intrusion.
incidents.impact: Province's election agency sued to force takedown of the searchable file. Highlights insider/political-misuse risk distinct from criminal breaches.

incidents.vector: Unknown intrusion vector; Trellix said no changes were made to its products and it has notified law enforcement and Europol.
incidents.impact: Attackers obtained source code for the security vendor's products; raises follow-on supply-chain and reverse-engineering risk for Trellix customers and Europol partners.

incidents.vector: Unspecified intrusion against the CNAM healthcare database. No ransom demand was made — atypical of cybercrime — and Moldova's cyber agency did not rule out Russian involvement.
incidents.impact: Personal and financial information of nearly every adult Moldovan and details of partnered private medical providers were stolen; ~30% of the database was affected. CNAM says payments to providers continued on schedule. Incident comes amid Russian threats of military intervention and ongoing accusations of Russian cyber/disinformation pressure on Chișinău.

incidents.victim: Cuban Embassy in Washington (and 5,000+ Microsoft Exchange servers globally)
incidents.vector: Chinese intrusion set breached a Microsoft Exchange email server at Cuba's DC embassy and exfiltrated diplomatic inboxes; the same campaign compromised more than 5,000 Exchange servers worldwide.
incidents.impact: Beijing reportedly used the access to spy on US naval-blockade-related diplomatic traffic moving through the Cuban mission, providing geopolitical intelligence on US military posture in the Caribbean.

incidents.victim: Delta Dental Insurance Company / Delta Dental of New York
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — data extortion (Cl0p / MOVEit campaign)
incidents.vector: 2023 zero-day exploitation of Progress MOVEit Transfer servers used by DDIC/DDNY to exchange files with affiliates and providers; attackers exfiltrated names, addresses, SSNs, driver's license numbers, financial account info and patient health data.
incidents.impact: NYDFS announced a $2.25M settlement on April 30, 2026, finding DDIC/DDNY's cybersecurity program non-compliant with 23 NYCRR Part 500 and faulting incident-reporting timeliness. Notification to affected consumers had been completed by March 2024.

incidents.vector: Unspecified intrusion that exfiltrated internal documents from Mediaworks (Hungary's largest private news agency).
incidents.impact: Leaked editorial meeting notes revealed content directors said they would 'contact Moscow' for help publishing anti-Ukraine material — evidencing Russia–Hungary propaganda coordination. The leak landed weeks after the pro-Kremlin governing party lost national elections. Mediaworks is suing publications that covered the leak.

incidents.vector: Voice-phishing (vishing) of an ADT employee yielded their Okta single-sign-on credentials, which the attackers used to pivot into ADT's Salesforce instance.
incidents.impact: Personal information on 5.5 million customers was exfiltrated and put up for extortion — part of an ongoing ShinyHunters spree that also recently hit Medtronic, Rockstar Games, McGraw Hill, 7-Eleven, Zara, Udemy and Carnival.

incidents.vector: Same ShinyHunters campaign approach (typically voice-phishing of IT/help-desk staff and SaaS pivoting); specific entry vector not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Personal data on 7.5 million Carnival customers was leaked online after the cruise-line operator declined to pay extortion. Carnival is part of the cluster of ShinyHunters victims being weaponized in May 2026.

incidents.vector: An unauthenticated production API on Schemata's AI virtual-training platform left service-member records and sensitive military training documents exposed; the company took 150 days to remediate after being notified by Strix.
incidents.impact: US service-member personal records and military training material were accessible to anyone with a URL. Exposure is high-value for foreign intelligence collection.

incidents.vector: Attackers accessed Braintrust's AWS infrastructure, including its API-key database.
incidents.impact: Braintrust ordered customers — including Cloudflare, Vercel, Stripe and other major tech firms — to rotate API keys; raises supply-chain risk for any organization using Braintrust's AI observability tooling.

incidents.vector: Attackers compromised the official DAEMON Tools distribution site for nearly a month and embedded hidden backdoors in the installers.
incidents.impact: Anyone who downloaded DAEMON Tools during the compromise window received backdoored binaries; AVB has now released clean versions. Classic vendor supply-chain compromise that extends attacker access to downstream user machines.

incidents.vector: Microsoft Digital Crimes Unit, Europol and industry partners executed a coordinated takedown of Tycoon2FA's hosting infrastructure, the leading AiTM kit that bypasses non-phishing-resistant MFA.
incidents.impact: March 2026 disruption cut Tycoon2FA email volume 15% and sharply reduced victim reachability to active phishing pages. The kit has partially recovered by shifting to .RU TLDs and away from Cloudflare hosting — a positive but partial win for defenders.

incidents.vector: Mirai-variant botnet of TP-Link Archer AX21 routers vulnerable to CVE-2023-1389 was used to launch DNS-reflection DDoS attacks; the operator pivoted through Huge Networks (a Brazilian DDoS-mitigation provider whose CEO's SSH keys were stolen after a January 2026 compromise) and Digital Ocean infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Sustained DDoS campaign targeting Brazilian ISPs that are largely not Huge Networks customers; the Huge Networks CEO denies attacking competitors to drum up business and blames a 'dishonest competitor' who allegedly stole his keys. Each /16 prefix was hit for 10–60 seconds with four parallel processes.

incidents.vector: Attacker compromised an administrator account and set the delay on admin actions to zero, enabling instant malicious transactions across the platform's multi-blockchain integration.
incidents.impact: $5 million in crypto assets stolen from Wasabi Protocol — one of several DeFi heists in the period (Ekubo: $1.4M; Giddy: $1.3M; Purrlend: $1.5M), with crypto platforms losing over $606M in the prior 18 days.
